name: Recursive Teaching Dimension / Degeneracy
details: For every finite binary class, recursive teaching dimension dominates the degeneracy of its $1$-inclusion graph.
proof: For every nonempty subfamily $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$, the minimum teaching-set size of $\mathcal G$ is at least the minimum degree of its $1$-inclusion graph. Taking the maximum over all subfamilies gives $\max_{\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H}\mathrm{TS}_{\min}(\mathcal G)\ge\max_{\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H}\mathrm d_{\min}(\mathcal G)$. The left-hand side is $\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal H)$ and the right-hand side is the degeneracy.
proof_source: Corollary \ref{cor:rtd-degeneracy} in the survey, combining the max-over-subfamilies characterization of recursive teaching dimension with Lemma \ref{lem:teaching-set-degree-lower-bound}.
witness_verification: For the two constant concepts on any domain of size at least two, $\mathrm{RTD}=1$, whereas their $1$-inclusion graph has no edges and degeneracy zero.
